verdict.rationale: Kong is positioned as an MCP gateway. Its docs describe an MCP Traffic Gateway that governs, secures and observes MCP traffic, and a Catalog that inventories MCP servers. So you can register MCP servers with Kong and front them, but Kong proxies and governs their tools rather than consuming them itself the way an agent would. Missing for 10: evidence that Kong itself calls or uses tools from attached MCP servers, detailed docs on registering upstream third-party MCP servers, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
